newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Intria parent in Penang bridge project.
newsitem.headline: Intria parent in Penang bridge project.

text.p: Mekar Idaman Sdn Bhd, the parent of Malaysian construction company Intria Bhd, has been asked to submit a proposal to the Public Works Ministry to build additional lanes on the Penang bridge, the longest in Asia.
Works Minister Samy Vellu said on Sunday that Mekar Idaman, the bridge concessionaire, would be asked to submit a proposal for the widening, the national news agency Bernama said.
The proposal would involve building an additional lane on each side of the bridge, which was erected in 1985 to connect northern Penang island to the mainland.
"By 2003 or 2004, the third lane has to be completed to ease traffic congestion," said Vellu.
The 13.5-km (8.4-mile) bridge is the longest in Asia and third longest in the world, Bernama said.
Mekar Idaman owns 53.9 percent of Intria.
